Subject: Internal: initial findings for NorthPeak uptick

Team — quick internal notes from the bridge (summarized):
- Timeline: 07:48 UTC sudden increase in concurrent sessions from a small set of client IP ranges.
- Symptom: KV-cache miss rate spiked (prefix caching). Host-side CPU on pool-gpu-04 went to 95% and request queueing increased, which propagated latency.
- Errors: Two distinct stack traces observed — OOM on older quantization path and a small route mis-route returning 502 from our proxy layer when the backend queue exceeded threshold.

Immediate mitigations applied (07:55–08:10):
- Diverted NorthPeak traffic to dedicated warm pool (reduced backend queueing).
- Bumped concurrency limit and enabled aggressive prefix caching for their keyspace.
- Rolled temporary kernel-path toggle to avoid the older quantized path (avoids OOM).

Next steps (owner):
- Karthik: validate quantization path patch & run preflight on canary.
- Jordan: follow up on proxy queue thresholds and produce a short patch to reject gracefully before 502 cascade.
- Naomi/Marissa: prepare an exec readout and commitments list for NorthPeak leadership.

I'll assemble a technical RCA draft by EOD.

— Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
